title: Have a good trip!
goal: Say goodbye, look back, and close this course by weaving three times into one story — helped by one new tense, the *imperfect*, for painting the background and past habits.
bekal: recognize and use the most common imperfect forms: *eram, aveam, locuiam, mergeam*
tell background (*imperfect*) from events (*perfect compus*), and say "for a year now" with *de* + the present
use the right goodbyes and good wishes for every occasion

dialogs.title: Dialogue — La aeroport
dialogs.intro: Late July. Budi has been working in Bucharest for exactly a year, and now he's going home to Bandung for a month's vacation. Ioana and Andrei take him to Otopeni airport.

notes: **Când eram copil, locuiam în Bandung.** These two verbs are in the **imperfect** — a past tense that doesn't tell events but paints **situations or habits** that went on back then. English marks this with "used to", "was …-ing", or just "back then". Compare *am învățat multe* (perfect compus): that's a finished result you can count.

**Când ai venit, nu vorbeai românește.** One sentence, two tenses, two jobs: *ai venit* is the **event** (one point on the timeline), *nu vorbeai* is the **background** (the situation at that moment). That's how the two tenses almost always work together.

**Locuiesc în România de un an.** Look at the tense: **present**, not past — where English says "I *have been* living". For Romanian, if you still live here the action isn't over — so it's the present, plus *de* + a length of time. *Am locuit în România un an* would mean you **no longer** live here.

**Ți-e dor de casă?** *Dor* is the word Romanians proudly call untranslatable: a longing that is sweet and painful at once. The pattern is the dative of feelings from unit 17: *mi-e dor de* + what you miss. *Mi-e dor de tine* = I miss you. And *nu-mi vine să cred* ("I can't believe it") is a fixed phrase — learn it whole.

**Salută-i! Să ne scrii!** Two ways to tell someone to do something. The first is the imperative from unit 17, with the pronoun attached at the end (*-i* = them). The second is *să* + subjunctive, which sounds softer — more a wish than an order: *Să ne scrii!* "be sure to write to us", *Să ai grijă de tine!* "take care of yourself".

grammars.title: The imperfect — the tense for background and habits
body: The imperfect is the most regular past tense in Romanian: one set of endings for every verb, **-am, -ai, -a, -am, -ați, -au**, with almost no exceptions. At A1 you only need to **recognize** it and use a few of the most common forms.
after: **How to form it:** *-a* verbs take **-am** (*a lucra → lucram*, *a mânca → mâncam*); *-ea, -e*, and *-i* verbs take **-eam** (*a avea → aveam*, *a face → făceam*, *a vorbi → vorbeam*, *a dormi → dormeam*); and *-i* after a vowel takes **-iam** (*a locui → locuiam*; likewise *a ști → știam*). Irregulars to remember: *a fi → eram*, *a da → dădeam*, *a sta → stăteam*, *a vrea → voiam*.
**The *eu* and *noi* forms are identical.** Context tells them apart, and if needed the pronoun is added: *Eu eram obosit, dar noi toți eram fericiți.*

**When the imperfect, when the perfect compus?** The imperfect for habits (*În fiecare vară mergeam la mare*), states (*Era frig. Aveam zece ani. Nu știam nimic.*), and actions **in progress** when something happened. The perfect compus for finished events: *Citeam când **a sunat** Ioana.* — "I was reading when Ioana called." *Ploua când **am ajuns** la aeroport.*

Dative states change too: *mi-e frică → mi-era frică*, *mi-e foame → mi-era foame*. And *a fost* from unit 14 is still used for a final verdict: *Era frumos* (it was lovely at the time — background) versus *A fost frumos* (it was a lovely event — conclusion).

grammars.title: "For a year now" — de + length of time, and a map of the three times
body: English uses the present perfect for two different things: "I *have eaten*" (finished) and "I *have lived* here for a year" (still going on). Romanian splits them sharply — and this is the last trap in the course.

head: Sentence
Tense
Meaning
rows: I've been living here for a year (and still am).
I lived there for a year (it's over).
I've been learning Romanian for six months.
I've been waiting for you for an hour!
How long have you worked here? — Since March.
***Acum** un an am venit în România.*
A year ago I came to Romania.
***Peste** o lună o să mă întorc.*
In a month I'll be back.

after: **Three little words, three directions in time:** *acum* + length of time = ago (*acum două zile*, unit 14); *de* + length of time = for that long and still going; *peste* + length of time = in, from now (*peste o săptămână* — in a week).

**A map of the four tenses you now have**, in one story: *Când **eram** student, nu **știam** nimic despre România* (imperfect — background). *Anul trecut **am venit** la București* (perfect compus — event). *Acum **lucrez** aici și **vorbesc** românește în fiecare zi* (present). *La anul **o să învăț** pentru nivelul A2* (future).
If you're unsure which past tense to pick, ask: does this answer "and then what happened?" If so — perfect compus. If it answers "what was it like back then?" — imperfect.

sections.title: Reading: Budi's note to Mrs. Popescu

blocks.text: Mrs. Popescu wasn't home this morning, so Budi writes her a message from the airport waiting area. Read the Romanian column first without peeking at the translation — this is the longest text in the course, and you'll find you understand almost all of it.

head: Română
English
rows: *Vă scriu din aeroport, pentru că azi-dimineață nu erați acasă.*
I'm writing to you from the airport, because you weren't home this morning.
*Când am venit la București, nu cunoșteam pe nimeni și nu vorbeam românește.*
When I came to Bucharest, I didn't know anyone and I didn't speak Romanian.
*Dumneavoastră m-ați ajutat mult și mi-ați explicat totul cu răbdare.*
You helped me a lot and explained everything to me patiently.
*În fiecare duminică îmi aduceați sarmale sau cozonac.*
Every Sunday you used to bring me sarmale or cozonac.
*Locuiesc în apartamentul dumneavoastră de un an și mă simt ca acasă.*
I've been living in your apartment for a year and I feel at home.
*Acum plec în Indonezia pentru o lună, la familia mea.*
Now I'm leaving for Indonesia for a month, to see my family.
*O să mă întorc în septembrie și o să vă aduc un cadou din Bandung.*
I'll be back in September and I'll bring you a gift from Bandung.
*Andrei rămâne acasă și are grijă de flori.*
Andrei is staying home and looking after the flowers.
*Vă mulțumesc pentru tot. Cu drag, Budi*
Thank you for everything. Fondly, Budi

blocks.text: Now read it again and hunt for the tenses. The **imperfect** paints background and habits: *nu erați, nu cunoșteam, nu vorbeam, îmi aduceați*. The **perfect compus** records events: *am venit, m-ați ajutat, mi-ați explicat*. The **present** is for what holds now — including *locuiesc … de un an* and *plec*, which is really the near future (unit 16). ***O să*** is for plans: *o să mă întorc, o să vă aduc*. Notice too all the short pronouns you can now take apart: *vă scriu* (dative, unit 19), *m-ați ajutat* (accusative in the past, unit 15), *mi-ați explicat* (dative in the past), *îmi aduceați*, *mă simt* (reflexive, unit 17).

blocks.title: Writing to someone you respect
items: Formal opening: ***Stimată doamnă…*** (to a woman), ***Stimate domnule…*** (to a man). To a friend: *Dragă Ioana*, *Dragă Andrei*.
Formal closing: *Cu respect* or *Cu stimă*. Warm closing: *Cu drag* ("fondly") — just right for a landlady who has brought you food for a year. To a friend: *Pe curând!* or *Te pup!*

***Sarmale*** are sour cabbage rolls filled with minced meat and rice, a must at Christmas and celebrations. ***Cozonac*** is a sweet bread filled with walnuts or chocolate, baked for Easter and Christmas. A neighbor who brings you a plate of either is a sign you've become family.

head: Română
Say it
When to use it
rows: seeing off a traveler — "have a good trip"
the same, a bit more formal — "have a pleasant journey"
to someone leaving for a long time — "write to us"
parting after an introduction — "nice to meet you"

blocks.title: La mulți ani — one wish for many days
items: Literally "to many years". It's used for birthdays, New Year's Eve, the national day on December 1, and the ***ziua numelui*** — name day.

Many Romanians celebrate the saint's day of the name they bear: every *Ion* and *Ioana* on January 7 (Saint John), every *Maria* on August 15, every *Andrei* on November 30. That day Ioana and Andrei get *La mulți ani!* wishes and usually treat their coworkers.

On March 1 people exchange the ***mărțișor***: a tiny charm on a red-and-white string marking the arrival of spring, pinned to your clothes. The wish: *O primăvară frumoasă!* — "Have a lovely spring!"

sections.title: Twenty units, and what comes next

blocks.text: Look back for a moment. In unit 1 all you could say was *Mă cheamă Budi*. Now you can order coffee, haggle at Piața Obor, buy a ticket to Brașov, tell a doctor what hurts, invite a friend to a concert, and write a message using four tenses. That's A1 — and you got through it by reading and imitating whole sentences, not by memorizing tables.

What awaits at A2: the full imperfect, the conditional (*aș vrea, ar fi* — which you've been learning as chunks), the possessive dative (*îmi curge nasul*), and complex sentences with *care*. None of it is truly foreign anymore; you've already met it all as chunks. In the meantime, reread the dialogues in this course out loud, listen to Romanian music and radio, and don't be afraid of mistakes. Romanians rarely meet foreigners who want to learn their language — every sentence you say will be met with a smile. ***Succes și pe curând!***
Cover the Romanian column, read the English, then rebuild the sentence from memory.

head: English
Română
rows: I'm looking for a white shirt.
Can I try it on? (the shirt)
This one is cheaper than the other one.
It's the prettiest dress in the store.
*Este cea mai frumoasă rochie din magazin.*
